title: Associated character line-bundle quotient and section presentation
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $G,B$ be $F$-group schemes with homomorphism $i:B\to G$ [def-sc-group-scheme], and let $Q$ be an $F$-scheme with $\pi:G\to Q$. Let $\chi:B\to\mathbf G_m$ be a character, using the fixed group schemes $\mathbf G_m$ and $\mathbf A^1=\mathbf G_a$ of [def-sc-gm-ga]. Use the actual coordinate algebras, evaluations and semi-invariant submodules of [def-sfb-rho-section-module-data], and the sheaves of modules and their canonical pullbacks appearing in [def-sc-invertible-module]. Define an associated-character-line-bundle presentation as the following data and compatibility laws, without asserting existence. It consists of an $\mathcal O_Q$-module $L$, a specified trivialization $\theta:\pi^*L\simeq\mathcal O_G$, an $F$-scheme $V$, a projection $p:V\to Q$, and a flat surjective quasi-compact map $q:G\times_F\mathbf A^1\to V$ with $pq=\pi\operatorname{pr}_G$. For every $F$-scheme $S$, $g_1,g_2\in G(S)$ and $z_1,z_2\in\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)$, require $q(g_1,z_1)=q(g_2,z_2)$ if and only if there is $b\in B(S)$ with $g_2=g_1i(b)$ and $z_2=\chi(b)^{-1}z_1$. For every $x:S\to Q$ specify a bijection between $\Gamma(S,x^*L)$ and maps $s:S\to V$ with $ps=x$, natural under arbitrary pullback; when $x=\pi g$, the inverse of the pulled-back trivialization sends $z$ to the map $q(g,z)$. Specify algebraic left $G$-actions on $Q$ and $V$, with $p$ equivariant, satisfying $s\cdot\pi(g)=\pi(sg)$ and $s\cdot q(g,z)=q(sg,z)$ on every $S$. These formulas specify fibrewise linearity and the natural action on sections in the atlas. Define the section module as $\Gamma(Q,L)$ with the scalar map $F\to\Gamma(Q,\mathcal O_Q)$, and its coordinate map as pullback followed by $\theta$. The affine-line point, inverse-character scalar, arbitrary-base trivialization and pullback maps in these laws are the canonical Spec--Gamma, inversion, and sheaf-pullback constructions, not arbitrary maps. Invertibility and coherence of $L$ are conclusions of the existence theorem, not fields assumed by this presentation.
